context:
Goal: a guard that refuses wrongly gets caught, not quietly worked around.
Problem (rule): no rule makes an agent or orchestrator check a refusal against the guard's record before taking another route; on Oct 31 three sessions routed around the builder-test refusal without asking. Asked in chat at 15:21 CDT.
Based on (read): rule verification-cry-wolf-guard-is-spent says a guard that cries wolf is ignored, but names no one who checks.
Based on (notes): lane merge-role-allow's report, Oct 31 about 14:20 CDT. That refusal turned out right; only the record's wording was unclear (step test-merge-conflict-role).

options.gain: False alarms get found and fixed instead of trained into habit.
options.how: Before routing around a refusal, the agent reads the guard's record; if the record seems to allow the act, its report flags a possible false alarm.
options.label: Add the rule
options.lose: One more CLAUDE.md line, and a little more work at each refusal.

options.how: Agents keep routing around refusals as now.
options.label: No rule
options.lose: A wrong refusal can be worked around for a long time unseen.

ref: test-merge-conflict-role (who resolves a test-file conflict); rule verification-cry-wolf-guard-is-spent
title: Must an agent check a guard's record before routing around a refusal?
why: This case was a right refusal with unclear wording, and the check is what found that.
